When you come back, one question greets you rather than a pile: whether to close, in one go, the applications that went quiet while you were away. Closing them is reversible; "Not now" brings the card back as it was. You can end the break from your profile at any time.

trackedJobs.title: Note jobs you haven't applied to yet
trackedJobs.intro: Tracked Jobs is a lightweight watchlist for jobs you're interested in but haven't applied to yet. Unlike an Application, it has no status, timeline, or employment type — just company, title, location, job URL, and your notes.

step1.title: Open "Tracked Jobs"
step1.body: Available from the top navigation.

step2.title: Enter the company name and job title
step2.body: Optionally add the location, job URL, and your own notes.

step3.title: Save it
step3.body: The job appears in your list with the date it was added.

step1.title: Click "Mark as Applied" next to the job
step1.body: This opens a small inline form.

step2.title: Enter the employment type and applied date
step2.body: You can add extra notes too.

step3.title: Confirm
step3.body: The job is removed from your tracked list and created as a real Application — you're taken straight to its detail page.

remove.title: Remove a job
remove.body: If you're no longer interested, "Remove" deletes it from the list permanently.

calloutNoEdit.title: There's no direct edit
calloutNoEdit.body: There's currently no way to edit a tracked job's details. If something's wrong, remove it and re-add it; if you've already applied, converting it with "Mark as Applied" and then editing the resulting Application is the way to fix the details.

applications.title: Create, track, edit, and delete your applications
applications.intro: Applications are the heart of e-kariyerim: each one has its own status, timeline, and (if available) job description.

step1.title: Click "New Application" from the Dashboard or Applications page

step2.title: Start typing the company name
step2.body: Companies you've added before are suggested as autocomplete; for a new company, just type it as-is.

step3.title: Enter the job title, job URL, location, and employment type
step3.body: The applied date defaults to today, but you can change it.

step4.title: Optionally add a source, a CV and notes, then save
step4.body: The source field can only be chosen when creating — it can't be changed later. If you have files on the My CVs page you can record which one you applied with; your default CV arrives already selected.

list.title: List, search, filter
list.body: The Applications list is paginated (10 per page) and supports searching by company/title, filtering by status, and sorting by date/company/title/status — all your filters are reflected in the URL, so you can share or bookmark a view.

detail.title: Application detail
detail.body: Opening an application shows its status badge, location, employment type, applied date, when it was added, the job URL (if any), the CV you recorded it with and your notes, with the Timeline and — if available — the job description below. Applications created automatically via Gmail Scanning show a "Created from Email" badge.

contact.title: HR contact and company links
contact.body: Under "Contact", an application can hold the person to follow up with — name, email address and LinkedIn profile. You can type them in yourself; the extension fills them in from the hiring-team card when a LinkedIn posting shows one, and confirming an email suggestion adds the sender's address the same way. Beside it the company's own website, LinkedIn and kariyer.net pages appear, along with its industry and country once they can be worked out. All of it is yours alone to see — e-kariyerim never writes to that person on your behalf.

edit.title: Editing
edit.body: "Edit" on the detail page lets you update the job title, job URL, location, employment type, applied date, and notes. The company name and source can't be changed after creation.

delete.title: Deleting
delete.body: Clicking "Delete" on the detail page opens a confirmation dialog — nothing is deleted until you confirm. To clear out several at once, select them on the list instead (see "Acting on many applications at once").

calloutConfirm.title: Deletion can't be undone
calloutConfirm.body: Deleting an application permanently removes its entire history, including its timeline.

step1.title: Click "Change Status" on the detail page

step2.title: Pick the new status from the list
step2.body: Your current status doesn't appear in the list — only the statuses you can move to.

step3.title: Optionally add a note and confirm
step3.body: The change is recorded in the Status History section as "Old Status → New Status", together with your note, which appears under that row.

statuses.title: What do the statuses mean?
statuses.body: An application can be in one of these statuses: Applied, Screening, Interview, TechnicalInterview, FinalInterview, Offer, Accepted, Rejected, Withdrawn, Ghosted.

timeline.title: Timeline
timeline.body: The detail page gathers everything that happened to an application into one chronological list, newest first: every status change and every event you added yourself. A status row says which status it moved from and to, when, the note you wrote at the time, and — most importantly — how the change was applied: whether you changed it yourself, confirmed an email suggestion, changed it as part of a bulk action, or undid one. For a change that came from an email, the rejection reason and the originating email's subject can be expanded inline.

addEvent.title: Adding an event yourself
addEvent.body: Not everything worth remembering is a status change. "Add event" records things like a recruiter getting in touch, a screening starting, an interview being scheduled or completed, an offer arriving, or a follow-up you sent — with the date it happened and a short note. Leave the date empty and it is recorded as now. The event joins the same timeline without moving the application's status.

companyView.title: Grouping by company
companyView.body: The List / Company switch above the list collects the same applications under the company you sent them to. In the company view a page holds 10 companies rather than 10 applications — so a company's applications are never split across two pages. Each company header shows how many applications you have there, how they are spread across statuses, and when something last moved; click the header to fold a group away, or use its checkbox to select all of that company's applications at once. Search and the status filter work the same way in both views, and the view you pick is reflected in the URL. If you have more than 20 applications at one company, the link under the group takes you to the flat list narrowed to it.

bulk.title: Acting on many applications at once
bulk.body: Tick the box on any row and an action bar appears at the bottom of the screen with two things you can do to the selection: change the status of all of it, or delete all of it. The box in the table header takes the whole page, and next to the count there is a link that reaches past it — every application the current search and filters match, not just the ten in front of you.

step1.title: Select the rows
step1.body: Row by row, a whole page at a time, or everything matching the filter. In the company view, the box on a group header takes that company's listed applications.

step2.title: Pick an action from the bar
step2.body: "Change status" moves every selected application to one status and can carry a note. "Delete" removes them.

step3.title: Confirm
step3.body: A status change asks once and tells you how many rows will actually move — applications already in that status are counted separately and left alone. Deleting asks for more: a tick to acknowledge it, and for "all matching" also the scope spelled out and the word typed in.

undo.title: Undoing a bulk status change
undo.body: After a status change, a strip stays on the list with an "Undo" button. It puts each application back where it was — except any you have moved on yourself since, which are left alone, because a decision you made later should win. The undo is added to each application's timeline rather than erasing the change it reverses: the mistake stays on the record.

calloutDelete.title: A bulk delete cannot be undone
calloutDelete.body: There is no recycle bin. Deleted applications, their timelines and the HR contacts attached to them are gone for good; the CV files themselves stay on the My CVs page. If you are not sure, export your data from Settings first.

suggestions.title: Automatic status suggestions from your emails
suggestions.intro: Once you turn on Gmail Scanning in the browser extension (see the Chrome Extension page), the system reads status-update emails you open and offers status suggestions — so you don't have to process every update by hand.

how.title: How a suggestion appears
how.body: Once a scanned email is processed, a card appears on the Suggestions page with the company, job title, received date, a confidence percentage, and a suggested status (if any). A suggestion that doesn't match a known application yet is marked with a "Not registered yet — new application from email" badge; if no clear status could be inferred, the card shows "Still pending" instead.

step1.title: Review the card
step1.body: Check the subject line and email snippet to make sure the suggestion is about the right application.

step2.title: "Confirm" to apply it, or "Dismiss" to skip it
step2.body: Confirm creates a new application (if it's new) or moves an existing one to the suggested status. Dismiss closes the suggestion without changing anything.

calloutConfidence.title: Check the confidence percentage
calloutConfidence.body: When confidence is low, read the email snippet first — automatic extraction isn't always exact, so you have the final say.

suggestions.gmailLink: How do I turn on Gmail Scanning? →

import.title: Bring in your LinkedIn history in bulk
import.intro: Right now the only import method is LinkedIn's own data export file (a .zip). There's no separate CSV uploader. Most of the work happens on LinkedIn's side; the steps below walk you through it end to end.

step1.title: Request your data export from LinkedIn — pick "Jobs" only
step1.body: On LinkedIn, open Settings & Privacy → Data privacy → Get a copy of your data. "Download larger data archive" takes 24 hours to prepare; choose the second option instead and tick only the "Jobs" box, and the archive usually arrives by email within 10 minutes. The "Job Applications.csv" we need for your application history is already in that selection.

step2.title: Download the .zip from the link LinkedIn emails you
step2.body: LinkedIn emails you once the archive is ready. Save the file to your computer and don't unzip it — the .zip itself is what you upload.

step3.title: Open the Import page in e-kariyerim
step3.body: Go to "Import" from the top navigation. The page walks you through the same steps visually.

step4.title: Drag the .zip into the upload area
step4.body: Drop the file onto the upload area, or click it to pick the file. As soon as it uploads, the status switches to "processing".

step5.title: Watch the progress live
step5.body: You'll see a progress bar with the number of rows processed so far; no need to leave the page.

step6.title: Review the summary
step6.body: When it finishes, you'll see how many new applications were added, how many were already there (duplicates), and how many rows couldn't be processed (invalid); any failing rows are listed individually.

calloutUnzip.title: Don't unzip the archive
calloutUnzip.body: The most common mistake is opening the zip and uploading the "Job Applications.csv" inside it on its own — that is rejected. And if you didn't tick the "Jobs" box when requesting the archive, that file isn't in the zip at all; in that case you'll need to request a fresh archive from LinkedIn.

calloutCsv.title: Only LinkedIn import is available
calloutCsv.body: There's currently no interface for uploading a hand-prepared CSV file. Applications created through import default to "FullTime" employment type, since LinkedIn's data doesn't specify one — edit the application afterwards if you need to change it.

settings.title: Account Settings
settings.intro: Settings is where you export your data, manage the browser extension's connection, see your Pro plan payments and open a refund request, and delete your account. Theme and language are switched from the top menu, not from Settings.

profile.title: My Profile
profile.body: My Profile in the avatar menu shows whose account this is and what it holds: your first and last name (editable), your e-mail address (cannot be changed; sign-in and notifications are tied to it), the date you joined, your plan, your latest reviews and salary entries, and your application, tracked-job and CV counts.

calloutName.title: The name is optional
calloutName.body: Sign-up does not ask for a name. Add one under My Profile and the top bar and our e-mails address you by it; leave it empty and the part of your e-mail before the @ is shown instead.

export.title: Export My Data
export.body: Download your applications (with their status history), your imports, your reminders, your CV records, the feedback you sent, your company reviews (with your reports and helpful marks), the salary entries you shared and your candidate experiences as a single JSON file. The CV files themselves are not in it; you download those from the My CVs page.

step1.title: Install the extension and click its icon
step1.body: See the Chrome Extension section.

step2.title: Press "Connect" and confirm on the page that opens
step2.body: There is no key to copy; the extension connects the moment you confirm.

step3.title: See and revoke connections here
step3.body: The "Browser Extension" section lists each connection's name, when it was created and expires, and when it was last used. "Revoke" invalidates it immediately.

step4.title: Entering a key by hand is still there, under "advanced"
step4.body: Only needed if you point the extension at a different API address. The key is shown once, and at most 10 can be active.

calloutToken.title: The connection only reaches the endpoints the extension uses
calloutToken.body: The key given to the extension can add applications, search companies and — if you turn it on — send email signals. It cannot export your application history or manage your account. Still give it only to your own browser: it expires on its own after 90 days, and "Revoke" invalidates it immediately if you ever have doubts.

billing.title: Plan and payments
billing.body: The "Plan and payments" section lists your Pro plan payments with date, amount and status; the "Manage plan and payment history" link takes you to the Pro plan page. No card details are kept by e-kariyerim: payment is taken on PayTR's secure page, so there is no card to delete or update here.

step1.title: See a payment's status
step1.body: Each row shows the plan, the payment date, the amount and the status: paid, pending, failed, refund requested, refunded. A pending payment can be followed on its result page via "Open"; you also get an e-mail once the result is final.

step2.title: Open a refund request
step2.body: Eligible payments show a "Request a refund" button; write your reason and send it (none is needed in the first seven days). You can also e-mail support@ekariyerim.com with your order number. We reply within 3 business days at the latest and e-mail the outcome. An approved amount goes back to the card you paid with through PayTR within 3–10 business days, and your Pro plan is wound back in proportion.

step3.title: Nothing to do to cancel
step3.body: There is no automatic renewal; we e-mail you three days before the end. If you do not extend, nothing is charged, Pro simply ends on its end date, and your applications and CVs stay exactly as they are.

calloutWithdrawal.title: Your right to a refund
calloutWithdrawal.body: Within 7 days of the payment date you get a full refund, no reason needed. After seven days the time you used is deducted, the rest is refunded and your Pro plan ends at that moment. We reply to your request within 3 business days at the latest. The details are on the Cancellation and Refund Policy page.

delete.title: Delete My Account
delete.body: Enter your password, type "DELETE" into the box, and click the button. A second warning tells you that all of your data will be deleted; once you confirm that too, your account and all of your data are permanently deleted.

calloutIrreversible.title: This can't be undone
calloutIrreversible.body: Once your account is deleted, everything belonging to it — your applications, your tracked jobs, your CVs, your imports, your reminders, your email suggestions and notifications, your company reviews, the salary entries you shared, your candidate experiences and the feedback you sent — is permanently gone; there's no way to reverse it.

chromeExtension.title: One-click application logging on LinkedIn and kariyer.net
chromeExtension.intro: The e-kariyerim Chrome extension turns a LinkedIn or kariyer.net job posting into a tracked application with one click — just press "I Applied".

install.title: Installation
install.storeIntro: The e-kariyerim extension is live on the Chrome Web Store — one-click install, no developer mode needed.

step1.title: Add the extension to Chrome from the link above
step1.body: Click "Add to Chrome" on the Chrome Web Store page. The extension icon appears in your toolbar.

step2.title: Click the extension icon and press "Connect"
step2.body: Sign in (or create an account) on the confirmation page that opens and confirm the code — there is no key to copy.

installManual.title: Alternative: unpacked install (developer/testing only)
installManual.intro: If you can't use the Store version — for example, you're testing an unreleased development build — you can also load the extension manually:

step1.title: Open chrome://extensions
step1.body: Just type it into the address bar and press Enter.

step2.title: Turn on "Developer mode"
step2.body: Found in the top right of the page.

step3.title: Click "Load unpacked" and select the extension folder
step3.body: The extension icon appears in your toolbar.

step1.title: Click the e-kariyerim icon in your toolbar

step2.title: Click "Connect"
step2.body: The extension produces a pairing code and opens the confirmation page in a new tab. If you are not signed in yet, you can do that there — the code is not lost.

step3.title: Check the code matches, then confirm
step3.body: The code on the page must match the one the extension is showing. Once you confirm, the extension connects within a few seconds. The connection is valid for 90 days; the extension warns you before it lapses, and renewing it is the same "Connect" button. If you point the extension at a different API address, entering a key by hand is still available under "advanced" in its settings.

step1.title: Open a LinkedIn or kariyer.net job posting page

step2.title: Click the extension icon
step2.body: It tries to auto-fill the company, title, and location from the page.

step3.title: Check the fields and correct anything that's off
step3.body: Auto-fill isn't always perfect — every field is editable before you submit.

step4.title: Click "I Applied"
step4.body: Your application is saved to e-kariyerim.

calloutScraping.title: Auto-fill is best-effort
calloutScraping.body: LinkedIn and kariyer.net occasionally change their page layout, which can leave some fields empty. That shows up as a blank field for you to fill in by hand, rather than submitting wrong data.

calloutDedupe.title: Clicking the same job again is safe
calloutDedupe.body: If you click "I Applied" again on the same job posting, it won't create a duplicate — the system finds your existing application by the job's URL and returns that instead.

gmail.title: Gmail Scanning
gmail.body: If you turn on Gmail Scanning on the extension's settings page, emails you open in Gmail that look like hiring correspondence (an interview invitation, a rejection, an offer) are recognised, and only the sender, subject, a short snippet and the date are sent to e-kariyerim — never the whole email. It ships off; until you turn it on, the extension never touches Gmail.
gmail.next: Every recognised email becomes a card on the Suggestions page, where you decide what to do with it. The details are on the Suggestions help page.

q1.question: What happens if someone gets hold of my Chrome extension token?
q1.answer: That token grants full access to your account. If you suspect it's been exposed, go to Settings → Browser Extension and "Revoke" it immediately, then generate a new one.

q2.question: Can I get my data back after deleting my account?
q2.answer: No. Account deletion can't be undone; your applications, your tracked jobs, your CVs, your imports, your reminders, your email suggestions and notifications, your company reviews, the salary entries you shared, your candidate experiences and the feedback you sent are permanently deleted. You can export your data from Account Settings before deleting.

q3.question: What if the Chrome extension reads a job's details wrong?
q3.answer: Nothing gets submitted automatically — every field is editable before you click "I Applied", the popup just gives you a starting point.

q4.question: Does Gmail Scanning read my whole inbox?
q4.answer: No. It's off by default, and once turned on it only reads an email you personally open in Gmail — never your inbox list, never a message you didn't open. The check runs on your device; only a short summary of an email that looks job-application-related is ever sent to e-kariyerim.

q5.question: Can I import a file other than my LinkedIn export (e.g. Excel/CSV)?
q5.answer: Not currently — the only import path is LinkedIn's own data export .zip file.

q6.question: Can I edit a job I'm tracking?
q6.answer: There's no direct edit for Tracked Jobs; if the details are wrong, remove it and re-add it, or if you've already applied, convert it with "Mark as Applied" and update the details on the Application edit page.

q7.question: How many Chrome extension tokens can I have?
q7.answer: Up to 10 active tokens at once. You'll need to revoke one you're not using before generating a new one.

q8.question: Why does employment type always show "Full-Time" on imported or extension-added applications?
q8.answer: Neither LinkedIn's export nor the job pages the extension reads specify an employment type, so it defaults to "FullTime" — edit the application afterwards if you need the correct type.

q9.question: Can I change or delete many applications at once?
q9.answer: Yes. Tick the rows on the Applications list — or use the "select all matching" link to reach every application the current filter matches — and the action bar at the bottom offers a status change or a delete.

q10.question: I bulk-changed the wrong applications. Can I undo it?
q10.answer: A bulk status change can be undone from the strip that stays on the list afterwards; applications you have moved on yourself since are left where they are. A bulk delete cannot be undone — which is why it asks for a tick, and for the word typed in when it covers everything matching a filter.

q11.question: Is my CV shown to employers?
q11.answer: No. Files on the My CVs page are visible only to you, are never sent to a third party or to any AI service, and are not read or analysed (the one exception: if you turn on the paid weekly job matching and give separate consent, the text of your default CV is sent to Google Cloud Vertex AI to be compared with postings; details in the "Weekly job matching" section of the privacy policy) — recording which CV an application went out with is a note to yourself. The account-free CV scan doesn't store your file either, and the score is computed on our server; only if you tick the optional "writing notes" box is the CV text sent to Google Cloud Vertex AI, and it is not kept there. The details are in the "CV scan" section of the privacy policy.

q12.question: I have several applications at the same company. Can I see them together?
q12.answer: Switch the View toggle above the Applications list from "List" to "Company". A page then holds companies rather than rows, so one company's applications are never split across two pages.

q13.question: Is the company review I wrote anonymous?
q13.answer: Yes. A published review shows neither your name, your email nor the day; only the month and your relationship with the company (current, former, intern). Only moderators can see who wrote it, and only for moderation.

q14.question: Why isn't my review visible?
q14.answer: A review is published the moment you save it. If it is not on the company page, either a moderator took it down after a report — the reason is on the My Reviews page; edit it and it goes back to a moderator — or it was written before 16 September 2026 in the old free-text format and is still waiting in the queue.

q15.question: What can I use on e-kariyerim without an account?
q15.answer: Three things: CV Scan (your CV's ATS readability), the reply rate benchmark, and reading company reviews. Tracking applications, the dashboard, the Chrome extension and writing a review need a free account.

q16.question: What are weekly postings and what do they cost?
q16.answer: The Pro plan's feature: every Monday, new postings matching your criteria are compared with your CV and scored. Monthly or yearly, prepaid; the price is on the Pro plan page, VAT included; there is no automatic renewal.

q17.question: Is my CV sent to an AI?
q17.answer: Only for the Pro plan's scoring, only if you explicitly allowed it on the criteria form, and only to Vertex AI (EU). Otherwise your CV is never sent to any AI service; you can withdraw the consent at any time.

q18.question: Can I get a refund on the Pro plan?
q18.answer: Yes. Within 7 days of the payment date you get a full refund without giving a reason; after seven days the time you used is deducted, the rest is refunded and Pro ends at that moment. Open the request under Settings › Plan and payments or e-mail support@ekariyerim.com with your order number; we reply within 3 business days at the latest and the refund goes back to the same card through PayTR.

q19.question: How do I cancel the Pro plan?
q19.answer: There is nothing to cancel: Pro is a prepaid period, there is no automatic renewal and no card on file. We e-mail you three days before the end; if you do not extend, nothing is charged and the plan simply ends on its end date. Your data stays as it is.

q20.question: My payment was interrupted or failed; was my card charged?
q20.answer: If the payment window closed, you chose "Cancel" or your bank declined, nothing was charged; you can start the same plan again. If the result page says "verifying", we are waiting for the bank's confirmation: even if you close the page, we e-mail you once the result is final and it shows under Settings › Plan and payments. If your card was charged and the payment is still not recognised after a few hours, write to us via Feedback.

q21.question: Is the salary I share anonymous, and who sees it?
q21.answer: Yes. A salary entry never shows your name, e-mail or account; readers see the occupation you picked from the list, your experience as a band (0–1, 2–4, 5–9, 10+ years), your employment type, whether you are a current or former employee, the month and the amount. There is no free text. Only signed-in users can read salary entries; you can edit or delete yours on My Salaries.

cv.title: Keep the CVs you apply with in one place
cv.intro: My CVs is where you store the files you apply with. You can keep up to 10, download any of them, or delete them permanently. Your files are visible only to you.

step1.title: Open the My CVs page
step1.body: Go to My CVs in the top menu. Your files are listed on the left, and the selected file is previewed on the right.

step2.title: Pick or drop a file
step2.body: Tick the consent box, then press Upload CV or drag the file onto the dashed area below the list. PDF, DOC and DOCX are accepted, up to 5 MB per file.

step3.title: Watch your quota
step3.body: The counter next to the list heading shows how many files you have used. Once you reach 10, delete one before uploading another.

preview.title: Preview
preview.body: The first page of a PDF is shown in the panel on the right. That image is produced in your own browser — no copy of it is kept on the server. DOC and DOCX files cannot be previewed in a browser; download them to read them.

default.title: Default CV
default.body: Making a file your default means it arrives pre-selected when you record a new application. The first file you upload becomes the default automatically, and deleting the default passes it to your newest remaining file. You can always change the CV used field on the application form.

readability.title: ATS readability
readability.body: The "Measure ATS readability" button under the selected CV runs the same checks as the sign-in-free CV scan over this file: a score out of 100, the four category subtotals, the fix list and the text an applicant tracking system reads from the file. The report stays next to the CV; the list shows the score and "Open report" shows the detail. Upload the corrected version and measure again, and the old report is replaced. Uploading alone never measures anything; it runs only when you ask, and the report is deleted with the CV.

remove.title: Deleting
remove.body: Delete asks for a confirmation; once you confirm, the file is removed from the list and from storage permanently and cannot be recovered. Applications you recorded that CV on are not deleted — only their reference to it is cleared.

calloutPrivacy.title: Where are your CVs stored?
calloutPrivacy.body: Your files are held in a bucket closed to the public on Google Cloud in the EU region (europe-west1). They are never sent to any third party, AI services included. Because a CV can carry sensitive data such as a photo or health information, we ask for your explicit consent before each upload; the box is never pre-ticked. You can withdraw consent by deleting the file, and deleting your account deletes your files with it.

companyReviews.title: Company reviews
companyReviews.intro: What working at a company is actually like — anonymous, structured reviews from people who worked there and a score with a public formula. Reading needs no account; writing only needs a sign-in.

step1.title: Open the Companies page
step1.body: The Companies link in the top menu lists every company with at least one published review; the search box finds one by name.

step2.title: Open a company page
step2.body: At the top: the overall score, the averages of up to ten areas (work environment, management, career, work-life balance, pay, benefits, remote work, tools, hiring, onboarding), the star distribution and the statements picked most often; below them, the reviews. Sort by newest or most helpful.

step3.title: Know how to read the score
step3.body: A score appears only once enough reviews are published; until then the page says how many are still needed. An area average appears once enough people rated that area — until then you see the vote count. Every number carries the count it is based on.

write.title: Writing a review

step1.title: Sign in
step1.body: Writing a review needs an e-kariyerim account; reading does not. The "Write a review" button on a company page takes you to sign-in first, then to the form.

step2.title: Pick the company
step2.body: Choose the company from the list in the form. If it is missing, type its name to add it; an added company also shows up in other people's search.

step3.title: Rate, and pick statements if you like
step3.body: Your relationship with the company (current employee, former employee, intern) and an overall 1–5 rating are all that is required. Ten more areas can be rated or left blank. Once you rate an area, the form offers ready-made statements about it — pick up to five you liked and five that could be better. There is nothing to write.

step4.title: Publish
step4.body: Your review is published the moment you save it and appears on the company page and under My contributions. Readers can report it; if a moderator takes it down, the reason is on the My contributions page.

write.guideLink: How to write a fair and useful review →

calloutAnonymous.title: Reviews are anonymous
calloutAnonymous.body: A published review shows neither your name, your email nor the day; only the month and your relationship appear. Only moderators can see who wrote it, and only for moderation.

calloutModeration.title: No free text, one review per company
calloutModeration.body: A review is made of ratings and statements from a fixed list, which is what lets it be published on save. You can write one review per company; if your view changes, edit the existing one. There is a cap on the total number of reviews per account, shown on the My Reviews page. Reviews written before 16 September 2026 had free text; their ratings still count, their text is no longer shown.

manage.title: Editing and deleting
manage.body: The My contributions page shows the status of each of your reviews (published, pending, not published) and the moderator's note, if any; your salary entries and candidate experiences are on the same list, newest first. Edit changes the ratings and the statements; Delete removes it entirely, and a deleted review also drops out of the company's score.

report.title: If you see a review that breaks the rules
report.body: Use the "Report this review" link on any review card, pick a reason and leave a short note. Reports are looked at by a moderator; the review may stay up, the author may be asked to change it, or it may be removed. The "Helpful" mark feeds the sorting; neither a report nor a helpful mark reveals your identity to anyone else.

companySalaries.title: Salary information
companySalaries.intro: What people earn at a company — anonymous reports from people who worked there, with an occupation picked from a catalogue and an experience band. Reading and writing both need sign-in.

step1.title: Sign in
step1.body: Salary entries are only shown to signed-in users. The Salaries tab on a company page shows you the sign-in first if you are not, then brings you back to the same tab.

step2.title: Open the Salaries tab on a company page
step2.body: Each entry is one row: occupation, experience band (0–1, 2–4, 5–9, 10+ years), employment type, current or former employee, the period the salary was drawn in (e.g. 2021 – ongoing) and the monthly net amount; the annual bonus if any. Nobody sees the author.

step3.title: Know how to read the median
step3.body: Once a currency has enough current entries, the median and the lowest–highest range appear at the top; until then there are only rows. Entries current within the last two years count; older periods sit separately at the bottom of the list and do not affect the median. The median is not split by occupation — it is the middle of the current entries at a company.

step1.title: Open the contribution page
step1.body: In the top menu, Companies ▾ → Share salary, or the "Share a salary" button on a company page. Reviews are written on the same page; the switch at the top moves between the two.

step2.title: Pick the company
step2.body: The company is picked once and applies to both forms. If yours is not listed, type its name to add it.

step3.title: Fill in the form
step3.body: Occupation, total years of experience, employment type, current/former employee, the period you drew the salary in (years only; the last year too if you are a former employee), monthly net salary with currency, bonus or not — all required. The occupation is picked from a catalogue: start typing, find it by its Turkish or English name and pick it from the list; no entry can be made for an occupation that is not in the catalogue.

step4.title: Share
step4.body: The entry is visible to signed-in readers immediately. You are then invited to review the same company; you can skip that.

calloutAnonymous.title: Entries are anonymous
calloutAnonymous.body: Readers do not see your name, e-mail or exact years of experience; only the occupation, band, employment type, relationship and the years of the period are shown. The exact years are only in your own list and your data export.

calloutLimits.title: One entry per occupation, ten in total
calloutLimits.body: You can add several entries for one company under different occupations (a promotion, say); for the same occupation, edit the existing entry instead of adding a second. Ten entries per account in total; deleting frees a slot.

manage.title: Editing and deleting
manage.body: The My contributions page shows every entry you shared with its full figures, in the same list as your reviews and experiences. Edit changes the amounts and the period; Delete removes it entirely. An entry shared before the period was asked is listed under "previous periods" until you edit it.

cvScan.title: CV Scan
cvScan.intro: Applicant tracking systems (ATS) turn your CV into text first. This tool shows what an applicant tracking system can read from your file and gives a 0-100 readability score. No account needed.

step1.title: Drop your file
step1.body: PDF, DOC or DOCX, up to 5 MB. Drag the file in or pick it.

step2.title: Tick the consent box
step2.body: Consent is asked for every scan; the box never comes pre-ticked. A second, optional box asks for notes on the writing — the scan works fully and the score is identical without it.

step3.title: Read the result
step3.body: How the score splits across four categories, the raw text extracted from the file (in the order the parser saw it) and a fix list saying which page, which line and how many points each finding costs.

measures.title: What it measures
measures.body: Four headings: text readability, sections and dates, contact details, format and length. These are every parser's shared problems: if no text comes out, dates don't line up or the contact block looks empty, your CV goes missing in searches.

limits.title: What it doesn't
limits.body: It doesn't match you to a posting and gives no keyword score; it doesn't imitate any particular ATS; it says nothing about how you describe your experience. A claim like "you're a 64% match for this job" would be something we can't measure.

calloutPrivacy.title: What happens to your file
calloutPrivacy.body: The file is never stored; it lives in memory only for the duration of the request. The score is computed on our server and no AI model is asked for it. Only if you tick the optional writing-notes box is the CV text sent to Google Cloud Vertex AI, and it is not kept there either. What remains: your IP address (in memory for 2 hours for the scan limit; as a security record for 12 months, never linked to the score), an anonymous score and a counter. Details are in the "CV scan" section of the privacy policy.

calloutRateLimit.title: Scan limit
calloutRateLimit.body: At most five scans per two hours from the same connection. If you hit the limit, wait a little and try again.

benchmark.title: Reply rate benchmark
benchmark.intro: Enter how many applications you sent and how many got any reply; see your own reply rate next to your field's median. No sign-up, no email.

step1.title: Enter the two numbers
step1.body: How many applications you sent in the period you pick, and how many of them got any reply (rejections included).

step2.title: Pick your field and the period
step2.body: The sector comes from a fixed list; seniority and location are optional. No free text is collected.

step3.title: Read the result
step3.body: Your own rate, your field's median and what share of respondents sit below you. Your answer joins the pool anonymously and feeds the next person's median.

median.title: Median, not average
median.body: Because answers are anonymous, the same person can answer more than once or send a deliberate outlier; a median barely moves, an average does. The number comes only from what people typed into this form; it is never mixed with the application data the product collects.

scope.title: When the median is withheld
scope.body: A field's median is not shown until that field has enough answers; the threshold is stated in the tool's own "Where does this number come from?" section. If your field is below it, the overall median is shown, clearly labelled as such. Answers for short periods tend to look low: recent applications may not have had time to be answered.

calloutAnonymous.title: No identity is kept
calloutAnonymous.body: No email, no cookie, and no IP address on your answer's row. Your IP address is kept only in a separate security record of each submission, for 12 months, and is never linked to your answer. Fields come from fixed lists; nothing beyond your two numbers and your choices is stored.

calloutSignedIn.title: If you have an account
calloutSignedIn.body: The dashboard measures the same rate from your real applications: a record, not a statement. We keep the two apart; the benchmark tool writes nothing to your account.

weeklyJobs.title: Weekly postings and the Pro plan
weeklyJobs.intro: Every Monday morning the Pro plan searches LinkedIn and kariyer.net for new postings that match your criteria, compares each with your default CV, scores it, and spells out which criteria match and which are missing. Postings you already applied to are left out.

step1.title: Save your criteria
step1.body: Up to three job titles and one city. Remote-work preference and the e-mail digest are optional.

step2.title: Consent to your CV being scored
step2.body: Your CV is sent to the AI for scoring only if you explicitly allow it; without that consent the feature does not run, because there is no unscored version of it.

step3.title: Your list is ready on Monday morning
step3.body: Up to 50 postings that appeared on the two sources that week and match your criteria, ranked by fit score. A "N postings are ready" e-mail comes if you want it.

step4.title: One-click "I applied"
step4.body: A posting you apply to joins your application list and is never shown again in later weeks.

score.title: What the fit score is
score.body: A number from 0 to 100, produced by comparing the posting's text with your CV. Each posting also lists matched criteria, missing criteria and the required skills; the score is a measure for ranking and filtering, not advice. Postings under the minimum score you set in your criteria are hidden from the list.

plan.title: Price and period
plan.body: Monthly or yearly, prepaid. Prices are shown on the Pro plan page, VAT included. There is no automatic renewal: we e-mail you three days before the end; if you do not extend, nothing is charged, and no card is stored — payment is taken on PayTR's secure page and your card details never reach e-kariyerim.

refund.title: Refunds
refund.body: A full refund, no questions asked, in the first seven days; after that the time you used is deducted and the rest is refunded. Open the request under Settings › Plan and payments or e-mail support@ekariyerim.com with your order number; we reply within 3 business days at the latest and send the refund back to the same card through PayTR.

calloutConsent.title: Where your CV goes
calloutConsent.body: Only for scoring, only if you consented, and only to Vertex AI (EU region). You can withdraw consent from the criteria form at any time; from then on your CV is not sent. Details are in the privacy policy's "Job matching" section.

candidateExperiences.title: Candidate experience
candidateExperiences.intro: What a company's hiring process is like from the candidate's side — anonymous ratings from people who went through it, and the ready-made statements they picked. You don't need to have worked there; reading is public, writing needs an account.

step1.title: Open the Candidate experience tab on a company page
step1.body: The tab is public. On top: the overall score, the area averages, the rating distribution and the most-picked statements; below: the process statistics — outcomes, the typical length and number of stages, how many processes asked for an assignment.

step2.title: Read the cards
step2.body: Each card is one candidate's own process: the overall rating, the areas they rated, the statements they picked and short tags such as the outcome, length and number of stages. The date is a quarter; there is no job title, month or interviewer name.

step3.title: Know the threshold
step3.body: The score, the area averages and the process statistics appear once a company has at least three entries; until then only the count and the cards are shown. "Typical" values are medians.

step1.title: Open the contribute page
step1.body: Companies ▾ → Share an experience in the top menu, or the "Share your experience" button on a company page. Reviews and salaries are shared on the same page; switch between them with the control at the top.

step2.title: Pick the company
step2.body: The company is picked once and applies to every form. If yours is not there, type its name to add it.

step3.title: Fill in the form
step3.body: Only the overall rating is required. If you like, answer a few closed questions about the process (outcome, length, number of stages, interview types), rate the eight areas and pick ready-made statements for the areas you rated — up to five you liked, five that could be better. There is no free text.

step4.title: Publish
step4.body: The entry is published the moment you save. You are then invited to leave a review or share a salary for the same company; you can skip.

calloutAnonymous.title: Entries are anonymous
calloutAnonymous.body: Readers never see your name, e-mail, job title or the month you went through the process; only the ratings, the statements, the process tags and the quarter. Interviewer or team names are never asked anywhere.

calloutLimits.title: One entry per company, ten in total
calloutLimits.body: You rate a company's process once; if your view changes, you edit the entry. Ten entries per account in total; deleting one frees a slot.

manage.title: Managing your entries
manage.body: On My contributions you see, edit or delete your entries on the same list as your reviews and salary entries. They are deleted with your account and included in your data export.

ats.title: What an ATS is, and is not
ats.what: An ATS (Applicant Tracking System) is the software an employer collects applications in. It turns your CV into text, splits it into fields and makes it searchable by a recruiter.
ats.myth: "ATS software auto-rejects 75% of CVs" is not true. That figure traces back to a 2012 sales brochure; in a 2025 survey around 92% of recruiters said they set no automatic rejection rules at all.
ats.truth: The real risk is not rejection, it is disappearing: if the parser cannot read your experience, your CV never comes back in a search, your dates never sort, your contact field looks empty. That is exactly what this scan measures.

limits.title: What this tool cannot do
limits.noJobMatch: It does not match you against a job ad. No keyword score — "you are a 64% fit" would be a claim we cannot measure.
limits.noAts: It does not imitate one specific ATS. We cannot know whether Workday or Taleo is behind a posting; what we measure is the readability problem all parsers share.
limits.noContent: It does not judge your content. How well you describe your experience sits outside this score.

NoTextLayer.title: There is no readable text in the file
NoTextLayer.why: Your CV is a scanned image, or a file that carries its text as drawing. A parser cannot pull a single word out of it — not even your name reaches a search.
NoTextLayer.fix: Export straight to PDF from the program you wrote it in (Word, Google Docs, Canva). Printing and scanning it, or screenshotting it, destroys the text.

BrokenTurkishCharacters.title: Turkish letters are being broken
BrokenTurkishCharacters.why: The font cannot name its characters, or the Turkish letters are dropped on the way out. A recruiter searching for "Yazılım Mühendisi" will not find your CV.
BrokenTurkishCharacters.fix: Export the PDF in a way that embeds fonts (Word's "Embed fonts in the file", Google Docs' "Download as PDF"), or use a common typeface.

details.stripped: The text is Turkish but contains no ı, ş, ğ, ç, ö or ü at all — the letters were flattened to ASCII on export.

MultiColumnOrTableLayout.title: Two-column or table-based layout
MultiColumnOrTableLayout.why: A person's eye separates columns; a parser does not. It reads across the line and braids the two columns together, cutting your experience away from its dates.
MultiColumnOrTableLayout.fix: Move to a single column. Bring the sidebar content (skills, contact details) into the main flow, and stop using tables as a layout tool.

details.columns: A vertical band at {position}% of the page width that no word crosses — the signature of two columns.

SectionsOrDatesUnreadable.title: Sections or dates cannot be read
SectionsOrDatesUnreadable.why: A parser looks for headings first and date ranges second. An unrecognised heading means your experience lands in no field at all; without a range there is no timeline to sort.
SectionsOrDatesUnreadable.fix: Name your sections the ordinary way: Experience, Education, Skills. Give every role a plain range like "03/2021 - present".

ContactUnreadable.title: Contact details cannot be read
ContactUnreadable.why: The record created in the system has an empty e-mail or phone field. Even a CV a person liked has no address to reply to.
ContactUnreadable.fix: Put your e-mail and phone number on the first page as ordinary text — not in a header or footer, not inside an image, not behind an icon.

details.onlyInHeaderFooter: Contact details are only in the header or footer — many parsers never look there.

LengthOutOfRange.title: Length
LengthOutOfRange.why: In a long CV the relevant experience sits far down the file; in a very short one there is nothing for a parser to extract.
LengthOutOfRange.fix: Aim for two pages. Cut older roles down to a line, and stop repeating the same information in two places.

details.longEstimated: Around {pageCount} pages (a Word file's page count can only be estimated).

scoring.title: How company scores are calculated
scoring.intro: Every number on a company page can be checked against this page. Nothing is weighted by hand.

formula.title: The score
formula.body: A company's score is a weighted average of the Overall ratings in its published reviews, pulled toward the site-wide average until the company has enough reviews of its own. This is the standard “Bayesian average”; it exists so that a single 5-star review cannot put a company at the top of the list.
formula.n: n — the number of published reviews of the company
formula.avg: avg — the mean Overall rating of those reviews
formula.siteAvg: siteAvg — the mean Overall rating across every published review on the site
formula.m: {m} — the prior weight: the company is treated as if it started with {m} average reviews
formula.example: Example: three 5-star reviews with a site average of 3.5 give (3 × 5 + {m} × 3.5) / (3 + {m}) = 4.1, not 5.0. With thirty such reviews the score is 4.8.
formula.threshold: No score is shown until a company has at least {minimum} published reviews; the page shows the count instead.
formula.categories: Area averages (work environment, management, career, work-life balance, pay, benefits, remote work, tools, hiring, onboarding) are plain means of the reviews that rated that area, and each one is shown only once at least {minimum} reviews rated it — until then the page shows the vote count instead.

formula.topStatements: “Most often liked” and “most often could be better” count how many published reviews picked each statement, and show the top three; they appear together with the score, never below {minimum} reviews.

moderation.title: What gets published
moderation.structured: A review is ratings plus statements from a fixed list; there is nothing to write. That is what lets it be published the moment it is saved.

moderation.anonymity: Readers never see who wrote a review. Moderators can see the account behind it, which is what makes moderation possible.

about.title: A person applying for a job has valuable time too.
about.intro: e-kariyerim is the project of a team that has watched the same problem on the candidate side of job searching for years: people apply to dozens of postings, hear nothing back from most of them, and have not a single number to tell them what is going on. There was no tool on this side. We started building one.

problem.title: The problem we see in the industry
problem.story1: You prepared a CV, researched the company, applied; maybe you sat a test, maybe an interview.
problem.story2: Then you waited. A day. A week. Two weeks.
problem.body: Every hiring tool sits on the employer's desk: applicant tracking systems, job boards, filters. The candidate has an inbox and a guess.
problem.closing: We do not want this to become normal.
problem.closingNote: Even a rejection is worth more than silence.

aim.title: What we want to do
aim.body: Make the process visible from the candidate's side: track your own applications, see from real data how many were answered, measure how applicant tracking systems read your CV, compare your reply rate with your field's median, and read what people who applied before you say about companies. Let candidates' accumulated experience be a path for the next one.

items.time: People's time is valuable; candidates have a right to an answer.

subject.body: The subject of this agreement is the sale and performance of the Pro plan (the weekly job matching service) that the Buyer orders electronically through e-kariyerim (ekariyerim.com), and the parties' rights and obligations under Türkiye's Consumer Protection Law No. 6502 and the Distance Contracts Regulation. This text also serves as the pre-contract information form required by Article 5 of the Regulation; by ticking the box on the checkout page the Buyer confirms having received it.

service.title: The service
service.body:
The Pro plan is a service delivered digitally: every week, new postings on LinkedIn and kariyer.net are collected according to the job titles, location and remote-work preference the Buyer saved; if the Buyer separately consents, they are compared with the Buyer's CV and scored; and the Buyer is e-mailed when the list is ready. The scope and limits of the service (postings per week, source sites, scoring) are described on the "Weekly jobs" page of the help centre.
Term: the monthly plan runs for one calendar month, the yearly plan for one calendar year. The period starts when the payment is confirmed, or at the end of a Pro period that is still running. There is no automatic renewal and no card is stored; nothing is charged at the end of the period.
The service does not guarantee that postings will be found or that the Buyer will be hired; depending on the availability of the third-party sites, a week may bring few or no postings.

price.title: Price
price.body: The price is the amount shown in Turkish lira, VAT included, on the plan selection screen and the checkout page; there is no shipping, setup or other fee. The price at the time of the order is binding for that order; later price changes do not affect periods that have started. A receipt is e-mailed when the payment is confirmed; the invoice is issued with the details the Buyer entered.

payment.title: Payment
payment.body: Payment is taken in a single charge by credit or debit card through the infrastructure of PayTR Ödeme ve Elektronik Para Kuruluşu A.Ş. Card details are entered on PayTR's secure payment page; they never reach the Seller and are never stored by the Seller. If the bank does not approve the transaction, no order is created and nothing is charged. Card disputes (chargebacks) are handled between the Buyer's bank and PayTR.

delivery.title: Performance
delivery.body: The service is performed electronically; there is no separate delivery. The Pro plan is switched on in the Buyer's account as soon as PayTR confirms the payment, and the first list of postings is prepared on the following Monday. If the bank's confirmation arrives late, the service starts when it arrives and runs for the full term. By ticking the box on the checkout page the Buyer expressly consents to the service starting before the withdrawal period ends.

withdrawal.title: Right of withdrawal
withdrawal.body:
Under Article 15 of the Distance Contracts Regulation, the statutory right of withdrawal does not apply to services performed instantly in an electronic environment and started, with the consumer's consent, before the withdrawal period ends; the Buyer gives that consent on the checkout page.
Nevertheless, the Seller grants the Buyer the following contractual right: within 7 (seven) days of the payment date the Buyer may withdraw from the agreement without giving any reason; the whole amount paid is refunded and the Pro period ends. The right is exercised from within the app (Settings › Plan and payments › "Request a refund") or by e-mailing support@ekariyerim.com with the order number.

refunds.title: Cancellation and refunds
refunds.body: After the seven days the Buyer may still request a refund; in that case the time used is deducted: the refund is the share of the amount paid that corresponds to the remaining days of the period, and the Pro period ends with the refund. Requests are decided within 3 business days at the latest and the outcome is e-mailed to the Buyer. An approved refund is made only through PayTR, to the card the payment was made with; depending on the bank it appears within 3–10 business days. The details are on the Cancellation and Refund Policy page, which forms an integral part of this agreement.

obligations.title: Obligations of the parties
obligations.body:
The Seller undertakes to provide the service for the term as described in this agreement and the help centre; to process the Buyer's personal data in line with the Privacy Policy; and to answer refund requests within the stated time. Short interruptions from planned maintenance or from the third-party sites do not mean the service was not performed; if, for a reason attributable to the Seller, the service is not provided at all for more than a week, the Buyer may ask for the share of the price that corresponds to that time.
The Buyer undertakes to protect the sign-in details of the account; to give correct billing details at checkout; to use the service only for their own job search and in line with the Terms of Use; and not to copy the posting data in bulk or pass it on to third parties. In case of a serious breach of the Terms of Use the Seller may end the service; whether the share of the price for the remaining time is refunded then depends on the nature of the breach.

disputes.title: Disputes
disputes.body: This agreement is governed by Turkish law. Disputes within the monetary limits announced each year by the Ministry of Trade are heard by the Consumer Arbitration Committees of the Buyer's place of residence or the Seller's place of business; disputes above those limits by the Consumer Courts. The Buyer may first raise any complaint or objection at support@ekariyerim.com; the Seller answers within 3 business days at the latest.

effective.title: Entry into force
effective.body: By ticking the box on the checkout page the Buyer declares having read, understood and accepted this agreement and the pre-contract information form. The agreement is concluded when PayTR confirms the payment and remains in force for the Pro period. The version of the agreement and the time of acceptance are stored on the order; the Buyer can reach the text on this page at any time. Later versions do not affect periods that have started.

refundPolicy.title: Cancellation and Refund Policy
refundPolicy.intro: This page explains how cancellation and refunds work for the e-kariyerim Pro plan.

scope.title: Scope
scope.body: These terms apply to the monthly and yearly periods of the e-kariyerim Pro plan and form an integral part of the Distance Sales Agreement. Payments are taken through PayTR; refunds are made only through PayTR too.

withdrawal.title: Seven days, no questions asked
withdrawal.body: Within 7 days of the payment date you can ask for a full refund without giving a reason: the whole amount goes back and your Pro plan ends. This is a right e-kariyerim grants you on top of the law, independent of the statutory withdrawal right being waived because you consented to the service starting at once.

cancellation.title: Cancellation
cancellation.body: There is no automatic renewal and no card is stored; nothing is charged at the end of the period. You do not need to do anything to stop the plan, it simply ends when the period runs out. An order closed before the payment window completed, or one the bank did not approve, is never charged.

howToRequest.title: How to request a refund
howToRequest.body:
Two ways:
• From within the app: the "Request a refund" button next to the payment under Settings › Plan and payments.
• By e-mail: write to support@ekariyerim.com with your order number (shown under Settings › Plan and payments).
No reason is needed in the first seven days; after that a short explanation is enough.

decision.title: Review
decision.body: We reply to your request within 3 business days at the latest; the outcome is e-mailed. Requests within seven days are approved as they are; later ones are settled by the calculation above.

howRefunded.title: How the refund is made
howRefunded.body: An approved refund goes back through PayTR to the card you paid with; depending on your bank it appears within 3–10 business days. No refund is made to another card, another account or in cash.

partial.title: Refunds after seven days
partial.body: You can still ask for a refund after the seven days; the time you used is then deducted and the rest is refunded. The calculation: amount paid × remaining days of the period ÷ total days of the period. Example: a refund requested on day 10 of a ₺299 monthly plan is about ₺199. Your Pro plan ends the moment the refund is made — you are getting the remaining time back as money. Once the period is over there is nothing left to refund.

proAfterRefund.title: Pro after a refund
proAfterRefund.body: With every refund your Pro period is wound back in proportion to the amount refunded: all of the period that payment added for a full refund, the remaining time for a refund after seven days. Time from other payments is kept. Your data (criteria, posting lists) is not deleted; if you go Pro again you continue where you left off.

contact.body: For refund and payment questions: support@ekariyerim.com. Include your order number; writing from your account's e-mail address speeds things up. Phone: +90 266 265 45 99.

benchmark.title: How this differs from the benchmark
benchmark.body: The benchmark asks you for two numbers; this table is computed from tracked applications. The two are kept apart on purpose and never pooled into one average.

companies.title: Where are the per-company figures?
companies.body: A company's figures open on its own page once it reaches {floor} applications in the last 12 months. Tracking your applications fills both the sector row and the company page.

items.source: Source: applications tracked on e-kariyerim, counted as people update the status by hand or through Gmail scanning. Benchmark answers never enter this table.
items.sector: Sector: the industry label on the company's LinkedIn or kariyer.net profile, mapped onto the benchmark's 12 sectors. Labels we cannot read go in no row.
items.window: Period: the last 3, 6 or 12 months by application date. A status change that arrives late is written to the application's own period.
items.maturity: Maturity: applications younger than {days} days are left out of the response, ghosting and silence denominators, so a reply has time to arrive. First-reply time is taken from every answered application.
items.threshold: Threshold: a row needs at least {contributors} different people and {applications} applications, and closes if one person accounts for more than {share}% of them. Below the threshold nothing is shown, not even how much is missing.
items.definitions: Definitions: response rate = applications a human touched (rejections included); ghosted = the ones the user marked as ghosted; post-interview silence = invited to an interview and then ghosted, as a share of those invited; median first reply = days between applying and the first status change.
